Subject: Re: Inference errors and slowdowns on reserved pool — urgent

Quick technical readout (initial):

- Root cause signal: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 currently showing sustained saturation on a subset of nodes serving cb-fin-1. We observed a ~3x increase in per-request token generation time vs baseline starting at 15:40 PT. Telemetry indicates a simultaneous spike in KV-cache miss rate for cb-fin-1 (~60% -> ~85%), which increases autoregressive steps and breaks effective batching windows.
- Effect on reserved throughput: Token/sec delivered to the tenant is ~35–42% below the committed throughput for the last 20 minutes (consistent with customer report).
- Error mode: When the serving queues grow, we surface 502/504/5xx as upstream timeouts rather than graceful queueing.

Immediate mitigation options we can take (fastest first):
1) Temporary cross-tenant preemption: move noisy tenants off the affected nodes and push cb-fin-1 to reserved-only nodes for 24–48h. Requires exec sign-off for preemption and limited customer impact.
2) Emergency burst capacity: spin a short-lived burst pool (same region) and divert inbound traffic — this requires authorization for burst credits and node allocation. Expected to restore throughput to ~90% of baseline within 10–15 minutes of cutover.
3) Canary rollback: roll cb-fin-1 to previous model revision (smaller KV footprint / quantized checkpoint) for customers on reserved tier. This avoids infra changes but requires coordination and 10–20 minute deployment.
4) Aggressive prefix/KV caching tuning to reduce misses (medium-term; may take ~30–60 minutes to see benefit).

I'm attaching a short CSV of the telemetry slices (engineer-telemetry.csv).

Recommendation: authorize option (2) immediate + (3) canary rollback if we see persistent miss-rate after burst. Also ask Ops to throttle any noisy non-reserved tenants that are contributing to node pressure.

I'll stand by for exec direction so we can action immediately.

—David
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Thanks team — concise exec decision below.

Summary: Cobalt Bank (DEAL-4482) is experiencing reserved throughput shortfall in us-west-2 caused by a KV-cache miss spike and resultant serving queueing. The customer impact is high (checkout failures).

Decision (authorized immediately):
- Approve emergency burst capacity: provision up to +35% temporary capacity in us-west-2 for a 48-hour window. Finance, mark as non-standard burst credit pending later reconciliation.
- Approve limited cross-tenant preemption on the affected node set for a 2-hour remediation window (Ops to minimize noisy tenant disruption).
- Approve canary rollback of cb-fin-1 to the previous quantized variant if telemetry after burst does not show improvement within 20 minutes.

Sales / Customer comms: Rishi / Monica — notify Cobalt with timeline and offer a goodwill credit; coordinate wording with Legal if needed. Suggested customer message: we are provisioning emergency capacity and expect service restoration within ~15 minutes of cutover; we'll follow with a post-incident analysis and any credit.

Engineering / Ops: David — execute plan (burst + preemption) now and confirm when traffic has stabilized. Keep logs for RCA.

I'll join a short bridge if needed — ping me if any blocker.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability
